$comment: Prerequisite edges. `topicId` requires `prerequisiteId`. strength "hard" gates the knowledge frontier — a topic is not ready until every hard prerequisite is mastered. strength "soft" only orders the queue and does not block.

dependencies.reason: The subprocess explanation only means something once you know which loop the SDK took over
You cannot judge what query() gives you without knowing what it replaced
The comparison is between two entry points you must be able to name first
The claude_code preset is only intelligible if you know Claude Code is running underneath
systemPrompt is an options field, so it helps to have seen the options object
Reading settings off disk is a Claude Code behaviour, inherited because of the subprocess
A turn cap is meaningless until you know what a turn is in the loop the SDK runs
Budgets are set through the options object
Delegation is a policy decision, and policy is what you own once the SDK owns the loop
Knowing how one agent runs frames why you would want a second
Define agents only after you can say why one is worth its overhead
Filesystem agents in .claude/agents are subject to the same on-disk loading rules
The field list is the content of the programmatic definition form
You have to know the field names before the casing of the field names can bite
tools and disallowedTools are AgentDefinition fields
A defined agent still needs a tool call to spawn it
"Must be auto-approved" only lands once you know what allowedTools actually does
What crosses inward is defined against the fields that could have carried it
The parent's system prompt is one of the things that does not cross
The return path is the second half of the same boundary
run_in_background is an argument on the tool that spawns the agent
Detection means matching that tool's name in the stream
agentId arrives inside the tool result you learn to read there
Hub-and-spoke is forced by isolation: there is no sibling channel
Both shapes describe how the hub splits work
The defect being diagnosed is a decomposition defect
You reason about what the coordinator saw, which is only the final messages
Hooks are the policy half of the mechanism/policy split
Learn why code beats a request before memorising where the code attaches
The event list is Claude Code's, exposed through the SDK
You register against an event you can name
Direction is the Pre/Post distinction inside the event list
The return shape belongs to the callback you just learned to write
Which return shape is legal depends on which event, and direction organises the events
updatedInput and additionalContext are alternatives to the decision fields
defer is one of the four permissionDecision values
Permission modes are a Claude Code concept the SDK inherits
canUseTool fires only when the mode resolves to a prompt
The whole point is the contrast with a PreToolUse hook's decision
Unlisted tools fall through to the permission mode, so the modes come first
Custom tools are the tool half of the policy you now own
Servers are wired in through the options object
tool() defines the tools an in-process server holds
Annotations are an argument to tool(), in a different position per language
"Hints, not controls" needs a picture of where real controls live
In-process is one of the four mcpServers shapes
strictMcpConfig excludes exactly the on-disk sources settingSources governs
The description is the second argument you just learned to pass
isError is a field on the result your handler returns
The two conventions are defined against the one real field
A structured error is an error payload designed the way this topic teaches
What propagates to the coordinator is the subagent's final message
resume and continue are options on the entry point
The client manages sessions for you, so the contrast sharpens both
forkSession only means anything alongside resume
Automatic compaction is one of the things the SDK now does for you
PreCompact is on the event list
The lever works because only the final message comes back
It is the alternative to compaction, so both have to be on the table
A Stop hook uses the top-level decision: block shape
It is the principle applied to the end of a turn instead of a tool call
Capping the loop is the first line of the posture
Gating the outcome is the second line
Context exhaustion is one of the failure modes the posture has to cover
